title: Midian
lead: A people of tent-dwelling clans in northwest Arabia, traced to Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25:2). Midian was Moses' refuge and the home of his father-in-law Jethro, but later the enemy of Peor, of the war in Numbers 31, and of Gideon's day.

sections.b: Midianite traders sold Joseph to Egypt (Genesis 37:28, 36). Moses fled to Midian, married Zipporah, and met God at the burning bush while tending Jethro's flock (Exodus 2–3). Jethro advised Moses on judging the people (Exodus 18). Yet in Numbers Midian joins Moab against Israel (Numbers 22:4, 7), a Midianite princess is killed at Peor (25:6–15), and Israel makes war on Midian (31). In Judges 6–8 Midianite camel raiders oppress Israel until Gideon defeats them, and "the day of Midian" became a byword for God's victory (Isaiah 9:4).
